name: schemii-private-actor-v1
transport: AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET socketpair; native in-memory attachment only
sequence: Each direction starts at 1, exact next uint64, no wrap, duplicate or gap; ACK intent_sequence is strictly increasing observed opposite-direction sequence, never durability or terminal evidence
pressure: Nonblocking send/receive; 128 finite task slots; full send/slot/wrap/malformed/ancillary/peer loss latches UNKNOWN, no retry/reconnect or eviction of unresolved slots
highwater: Local observation only: all sent frames receipt-ACKed, no loss/gap/live task/helper/pending intent/wait. Reserved wire highwater refused; no CLEAN/network or restart grant

clone_policy.clone3_all_forms: ENOSYS before reading mutable args; legacy libc fallback permitted

fd_allowlists.owner: selected directory lease, journal/private state when implemented, Java control, both unexported actor endpoints
fd_allowlists.proot: 0,1,2 and designated actor endpoint plus explicit mount inputs only, future native custody transfer required
fd_allowlists.sysvipc_before_dup: 0,1,2 and two service pipe ends only
fd_allowlists.future_python: 0,1,2 plus designated guest lease only; no actor, journal, predecessor or owner controls; subprocesses close guest lease

authority: NONE: source producer only, APK C/A and all production births unconditionally refused
conversion: Java uses JNI scalar methods; the native internal pair carries four native-endian uint32 fields. Python FD3 uses 16-byte big-endian SCH1 frames (!4sIII); actor frames use 224-byte big-endian SCA1. These protocols are disconnected and production launch remains REFUSED. Future native custody requires an explicit versioned guest-lease conversion after genuine C/A and durable journal admission; no current handshake
guest_reservation: Accepted guest INTENT reserves one free slot and the next unique incarnation before kernel resume. Both channel ends derive it in exact INTENT sequence order; TASK attaches by that intent even when attachments arrive out of order. Only an observed negative birth result releases its reservation; lost or unresolved intents retain it. Native allocations and all guest creators share the same finite slots and counter; no wrap or unresolved reuse.
